full_article:
T he massive glacial collapse that caused catastrophic flash floods in the Himalayan border region of Nepal ⁠and Tibet has killed at least 165 people, though the number of dead is set to rise, with local officials saying more than 1,000 were missing.

Officials said 826 people were missing in Nepal, among them 579 tourists from two dozen countries, including India, the US, Australia, Britain and Canada. Chinese ‌state media said 558 people were missing ​in Tibet’s Gyirong ⁠county. It was not immediately clear if the missing counts were separate or some people had been counted twice.

At 8.37am on Wednesday, an enormous section ⁠of a glacier in the Himalayas sheared free and crashed on to the valley floor in Nepal’s Langtang national park, about 60km north of the capital Kathmandu, near the mountainous Nepal-Tibet border.

Map showing the flood-affected locations from the Nepal flash flood Map showing the flood-affected locations from the Nepal flash flood

Such was the force of the event, it was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. The United States Geological Survey later determined the tremor was caused ​by glacial rock and ice collapsing, registering a magnitude of 5.2.

The collapse triggered a huge release of water, mud, rock and ice that thundered down valleys and swept down the Lhende Khola, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers.

The high-speed flash floods careered towards northern Nepalese towns, including areas popular with mountaineering tourists and pilgrims.

Deadly flash flood hit Nepal and China

Horrifying videos from the Gyirong border post, which connects Nepal and Tibet, showed people running for their lives as the wall of debris obliterated buildings and swept away lines of buses.

In Nepal, houses and roads ⁠were washed away in seconds.

“It was a huge gush of mud coming straight towards us. As it got closer, it kept rising higher and higher. When I saw it enter our home, I tried to grab my wife’s hand and take ⁠her to the terrace. But she was swept away by the mud,” said Keshav Prasad Baral, a 68-year-old survivor, who was being treated at a small hospital.

“Four or five hours later, a helicopter came to rescue me. My wife is still somewhere beneath the mud. She’s gone.” Another survivor described being saved by clinging to a mango tree as he watched the house where he had been ⁠working disappear.

In a stark illustration of the deluge’s deadly power, a bridge crossing the Trishuli river was shown in a video being washed away in a tsunami-like flood. Multi-level homes were quickly submerged as the torrent gouged through the riverside town.

Flash flood destroys bridge and buildings along Nepal’s Trishuli river

Bibek Kumal, a Nepali labourer, was working in Bidur when others sounded the alarm. “I started running. Then a wall of water came thundering down as if it was an earthquake,” ⁠Kumal said from his bed at Kathmandu’s National Trauma Centre.

The torrent swept him downstream amid mud and debris, ​but “luckily I was stuck up in a mango tree, he ‌said. “Had there been no mango tree, I would ‌have been washed away to death.”

At a location just north of Kumal’s lucky escape in Bidur, a video shows an immense flood swallowing a river valley as it surges towards Betrawati Bazaar, an important historical and pilgrimage town.

Deadly flash flood shown sweeping through valley towards Nepali village

Mud and water moving at such high speeds forms a lethal combination “like liquid concrete,” said Hatim Sharif, a hydrologist at the University of Texas San Antonio, adding that it cannot be outrun.

Satellite view of flooding in Betrawoti Bazaar, Nepal

Nepal’s tourism ministry said hundreds of people were believed to have been trekking in Rasuwa, one of the worst hit districts. Officials said 133 tourists ‌from India and the Indian diaspora were missing, as they made their pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.

Rescue operations were difficult on Wednesday because of damage to infrastructure and higher than normal river levels. Helicopters could not land in Nepal’s affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the Rasuwa region, which has a population of about 50,000.

Rescuers waded through mud and sludge, looking for survivors after flood waters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings.

View image in fullscreen Rescuers carry a victim of the flash flooding to safety along the Trishuli River in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: Niranjan Shrestha/AP

“There is devastation everywhere we ​look,” Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa, told Reuters. “The settlements next to ​the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.”

Dave Petley, an earth scientist with Nottingham Trent University, described the scale of the event as close to “apocalyptic”. The huge volume of water was possibly a combination of ice that converted to water as a result of the initial collapse and river water. But until the exact cause of the disaster could be confirmed by scientists, that was just speculation, he noted in the science outlet Eos.

The Himalayan mountain range spans several countries in South Asia and has many of the world’s highest peaks and remaining glaciers.

Satellite view of flooding

The steep slopes and the lush valleys below are especially vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events like intense monsoons and melting glaciers have become more common because of warming due to human-caused climate change.

View image in fullscreen An aerial view shows houses deluged in sludge after flash floods at Devighat, Bidur municipality in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: Prabin Ranabhat/AFP/Getty Images

Researchers in Kathmandu found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting faster, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000.

नेपाल केरऽ हिमालयी सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र म॑ विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ के कारण बनलऽ भारी हिमनदी केरऽ पतन ⁠आरू तिब्बत म॑ कम स॑ कम १६५ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै, हालांकि मृतक के संख्या बढ़ै वाला छै, स्थानीय अधिकारी सिनी के कहना छै कि १,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै ।

अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे 826 गोटे लापता अछि, जाहि मे भारत, अमेरिका, ऑस्ट्रेलिया, ब्रिटेन आ कनाडा सहित दू दर्जन देशक 579 पर्यटक शामिल अछि। चीनी सरकारी मीडिया के कहनाय छनि जे तिब्बत के ग्यरोंग ⁠काउंटी मे ५५८ लोक लापता अछि. तत्काल स्पष्ट नहि भेल जे लापता गिनती अलग-अलग अछि या किछु लोकक गिनती दू बेर भेल अछि।

बुधदिन भोर ८.३७ बजे हिमालय केरऽ एगो ग्लेशियर केरऽ एगो विशाल खंड ⁠के मुक्त कतरनी करी क॑ राजधानी काठमांडू स॑ करीब ६० किलोमीटर उत्तर म॑ स्थित नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा के पास नेपाल केरऽ लंगटांग राष्ट्रीय उद्यान म॑ घाटी केरऽ तल प॑ गिरी गेलै ।

नेपाल के आकस्मिक बाढ़ से बाढ़ प्रभावित स्थानों को दिखाने वाला नक्शा नेपाल के आकस्मिक बाढ़ से बाढ़ प्रभावित स्थानों को दिखाने वाला नक्शा |

एहन बल छल एहि घटनाक, शुरू मे एकरा 4.4 तीव्रता के भूकंप के रूप मे बताओल गेल छल. बाद मँ संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के भूवैज्ञानिक सर्वेक्षण नँ ई तय करलकै कि ई भूकंप हिमनदीय चट्टान आरू बर्फ के ढहला के कारण भेलौ छै, जेकरौ परिमाण ५.२ दर्ज करलौ गेलौ छै ।

एहि पतन के कारण पानि, थाल, चट्टान आ बर्फ के भारी रिलीज भ गेल जे घाटी के गरजैत छल आ ल्हेंडे खोला, भोटे कोशी आ त्रिशुली नदी के बहैत छल.

तेज गति स॑ आबै वाला फ्लैश फ्लड उत्तरी नेपाल केरऽ शहरऽ के तरफ बढ़लै, जेकरा म॑ पर्वतारोहण पर्यटक आरू तीर्थयात्री लेली लोकप्रिय क्षेत्र भी शामिल छेलै ।

नेपाल आ चीन मे घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ि

नेपाल आ तिब्बत के जोड़य वाला ग्यरोंग सीमा चौकी के भयावह वीडियो में मलबा के देवाल भवन के मिटा देलक आ बस के लाइन के बहाबय के कारण लोक के जान बचाबय लेल दौड़ैत देखाओल गेल अछि.

नेपालमे घर-सड़क ⁠सेकेण्डमे बहल।

एकटा छोट सन अस्पताल मे इलाज क’ रहल 68 वर्षीय केशव प्रसाद बरल कहलनि जे, “ई थाल के एकटा पैघ झोंक छल जे सोझे हमरा सब दिस आबि रहल छल। जेना-जेना ई नजदीक आबि रहल छल, ओ ऊँच स’ ऊँच उठैत गेल। जखन हम एकरा हमरा सबहक घर मे प्रवेश करैत देखलहुँ त’ हम अपन पत्नी’क हाथ पकड़ि ⁠ओकरा छत पर ल’ जेबाक प्रयास केलहुँ।मुदा थाल-कादो बहरा गेलीह।”

“चारि-पाँच घंटाक बाद हमरा बचाब’ लेल एकटा हेलीकॉप्टर आबि गेल, हमर पत्नी एखनो कतहु थाल-कादोक नीचाँ छथि, ओ चलि गेल छथि.” एकटा आओर बचि गेल व्यक्ति आमक गाछ पर चिपकल रहबाक वर्णन केलक जखन ओ ओहि घर के गायब होइत देखैत छल जतय ओ ⁠काज करैत छल ।

बाढ़ केरऽ घातक शक्ति केरऽ एगो शुद्ध चित्रण म॑ त्रिशुली नदी पार करै वाला एगो पुल क॑ सुनामी जैसनऽ बाढ़ म॑ बहलऽ वीडियो म॑ दिखालऽ गेलऽ छै । नदीक कातक शहर मे धार डूबि गेलाक कारणे बहुस्तरीय घर जल्दीए डूबि गेल।

फ्लैश फ्लड नेपाल के त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे पुल आ भवन के तबाह क देलक

नेपाली मजदूर बिबेक कुमार बिदुर मे काज क रहल छल कि दोसर लोक अलार्म बजा देलक। “हम दौड़य लगलहुँ, तखने पानिक देबाल गरजैत नीचाँ आबि गेल जेना भूकंप हो।” ⁠कुमल काठमांडूक नेशनल ट्रॉमा सेंटर मे अपन पलंग पर बैसल कहलनि।

धार ओकरा थाल-कादो आ मलबा के बीच नीचाँ बहौलक, मुदा “सौभाग्यवश हम आमक गाछ मे फँसि गेल रही, ओ कहलनि, “आमक गाछ नहि रहैत त’ हम मरि गेल रहितहुँ।”

बीदुर केरऽ कुमल केरऽ भाग्यशाली भागै के ठीक उत्तर म॑ एगो स्थान प॑ एगो वीडियो म॑ देखलऽ गेलऽ छै कि एगो नदी केरऽ घाटी क॑ निगलतें हुअ॑ एगो अपार बाढ़ आबी रहलऽ छै, जब॑ ई एगो महत्वपूर्ण ऐतिहासिक आरू तीर्थ शहर बेतरावती बाजार के तरफ बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।

घाटी के माध्यम स नेपाली गाम दिस घातक झटका बाढ़ देखाओल गेल

टेक्सास विश्वविद्यालय सैन एंटनी केरऽ जलविज्ञानी हातिम शरीफ न॑ कहलकै कि एतना तेज गति स॑ चलै वाला कीचड़ आरू पानी एगो घातक संयोजन बनाबै छै “तरल कंक्रीट के तरह” आरू कहलकै कि एकरा स॑ आगू नै बढ़लऽ जाब॑ सकै छै ।

नेपाल के बेतरावोटी बाजार में बाढ़ के उपग्रह दृश्य

नेपाल केरऽ पर्यटन मंत्रालय न॑ कहलकै कि सबसें जादा प्रभावित जिला म॑ स॑ एक रसुवा म॑ सैकड़ों लोगऽ के ट्रेकिंग होय के आशंका छै । अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, भारत आ भारतीय प्रवासी के 133 पर्यटक लापता छथि, किया कि ओ सब हिन्दू के लेल पवित्र स्थल तिब्बत के कैलाश पर्वत के यात्रा केने छलाह।

बुधदिन आधारभूत संरचना के नुकसान आ नदी के स्तर सामान्य स बेसी के कारण बचाव कार्य कठिन छल। करीब ५० हजार के आबादी वाला रसुवा क्षेत्र के नेपाल के प्रभावित क्षेत्र स्याप्रू बेसी आ तिमुरे में हेलीकॉप्टर नै उतर सकल ।

बाढ़ के पानी के बाद बहुमंजिला भवन के निचला मंजिल गाड़ला के बाद बचावकर्मी थाल आ कीचड़ के बीच सं गुजरल लोक के खोजैत रहल.

View image in fullscreen नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला के त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे फ्लैश फ्लडिंग के पीड़ित के बचाबय वाला के सुरक्षित स्थान पर ल गेल. फोटोग्राफ : निरंजन श्रेष्ठ/ए.पी

रसुवा के स्वास्थ्यकर्मी तुला बहादुर बीके रायटर के कहलनि जे, जतय देखैत छी तबाही भ रहल अछि। ओ कहला जे नदी क बगल मे बस्ती पूरा तरह स बह गेल अछि। हमर अपनहि पाँचटा रिश्तेदार गायब छथि।”

नॉटिंघम ट्रेंट विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ पृथ्वी वैज्ञानिक डेव पेटली न॑ ई घटना केरऽ पैमाना क॑ “एपोकैलिप्टिक” के करीब बतैलकै । संभवतः पानिक विशाल मात्रा बर्फक संयोजन छल जे प्रारंभिक ढहब आ नदीक पानि के परिणामस्वरूप पानि मे बदलि गेल छल । लेकिन जब॑ तलक वैज्ञानिकऽ द्वारा आपदा केरऽ सही कारण के पुष्टि नै करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै, ई खाली अटकलबाजी छेलै, ई बात क॑ हुनी विज्ञान केरऽ आउटलेट ईओस म॑ नोट करलकै ।

हिमालयी पर्वत श्रृंखला दक्षिण एशिया केरऽ कई देशऽ म॑ फैललऽ छै आरू एकरऽ दुनिया केरऽ बहुत सारा ऊंचऽ चोटी आरू शेष ग्लेशियर छै ।

बाढ़ के उपग्रह दृश्य

खड़ी ढलान आरू नीचें के रसीला घाटी खास करी क॑ बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन के शिकार होय छै आरू मानव के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण गर्मी के कारण तीव्र मानसून आरू पिघलतें ग्लेशियर जैसनऽ चरम मौसमी घटना अधिक आम होय गेलऽ छै ।

फुलस्क्रीन मे छवि देखू हवाई दृश्य मे नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला के बिदुर नगरपालिका के देवीघाट मे आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के बाद कीचड़ मे उमड़ल घर देखाओल गेल अछि. फोटोग्राफ : प्रबिन रानाभाट/एएफपी/गेटी इमेजेज

काठमांडू केरऽ शोधकर्ता सिनी क॑ ई साल केरऽ शुरू म॑ पता चललै कि पूरा हिन्दू कुश हिमालय क्षेत्र केरऽ ग्लेशियर तेजी स॑ पिघली रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ २००० स॑ बर्फ केरऽ नुकसान के दर दुगुना होय गेलऽ छै ।

title: "What Melts In Himalayas...": Nepal Minister Flags 'Common Threat' To India - NDTV
description: "What Melts In Himalayas...": Nepal Minister Flags 'Common Threat' To India  NDTV
publisher.title: NDTV
full_article:
"Whatever melts in the Himalayas rises in the sea," said Nepal Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal as he elaborated on the common threat to Nepal and India from the ecological fragility in the Himalayas.

Khanal emphasised on redefining India-Nepal relations in ecological terms while continuing to celebrate the cultural and religious linkages between the two neighbours.

"Nepal and India have always talked about our relations in terms of Roti-Beti, Sita-Ram . Religion and civilisational links have always played a big role in our ties. But we have to reframe our relationship in ecological terms," Khanal said at the NDTV World Anviksha Summit in Kathmandu on Thursday.

"What melts in the Himalayas rises in the sea. This is what we saw live in front of our eyes on Wednesday. A burst in the Nepal-China border region in the Himalayas sent water rushing downstream, devastating areas of Nepal," he said, talking about the devastating floods in the Himalayan nation.

"China, Nepal, India and Bhutan are connected by ecology and our shared survival and future depends on protecting the Himalayan ecology"

Calling for more ecological cooperation, the minister added that while this time the floods have not gone further downstream and impacted India, such incidents have happened in the past and may happen in the future.

"Fortunately, this time the floods have not gone further downstream to actually impact Indian areas bordering Nepal. But this has happened in the past."

In this context, the minister said that India, China, Nepal and Bhutan are connected by ecology and will have to keep their differences aside and work together.

"China, Nepal, India and Bhutan are connected by ecology and our shared survival and future depends on protecting the Himalayan ecology. There could be political rivalry, but we have to come together as the Himalayan region is most vulnerable to climate change," Khanal said.

Wednesday's flash floods had triggered alarm in areas of UP and Bihar on the Nepal border. The state governments had called emergency meetings and put administrations on alert to deal with any eventuality. Though the risk of impact was lower this time, the fears were real.

title: More than 1,300 are missing in Nepal and Tibet after catastrophic floods caused by glacial collapse - AP News
description: More than 1,300 are missing in Nepal and Tibet after catastrophic floods caused by glacial collapse  AP News
publisher.title: AP News
full_article:
DEVIGHAT, Nepal (AP) — Rescue teams searched on Thursday for hundreds of missing people along the Nepal-China border after a catastrophic and deadly torrent of floods and mud swept through several communities a day earlier following a glacier collapse.

The disaster left 168 people dead and more than 1,300 missing, including foreigners and pilgrims, and displaced hundreds of people across the Himalayan region.

Videos of the tragedy showed the flood swallowing people as they tried to escape, and destroying buildings and bridges. On Thursday, drone footage from Nepal showed the scale of the destruction.

The region’s steep valleys are economic lifelines and travel corridors, but are precarious when disaster strikes. Images showed what appeared to be the second floors of buildings in Nuwakot slathered in mud after the torrent rushed by. Debris hung from tree branches and wires, vehicles were buried and some stunned survivors were caked in mud. The floods halted travel in some areas.

There was little time for anyone to flee.

“When I reached Dhunge bazaar, in half an hour, the flood came and damaged all the market. People were preparing to go to the office then,” resident Shoyam Rajbhandari said. “How many people are missing or dead, we don’t know.”

Warming climate threatens communities

The Himalayan mountain range spans several countries in South Asia and has many of the world’s highest peaks and remaining glaciers.

The steep slopes and the lush valleys below the Himalayan mountain range are especially vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events. Melting glaciers have become more common because of warming because of human-caused climate change.

Researchers in Kathmandu found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting faster, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000.

Helicopters deployed as roads were damaged

The disaster has left at least 165 dead and 826 people missing in Nepal, and three dead and 558 missing in Tibet, authorities said.

Nepalese officials said that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometers (25 miles) of roads were damaged, complicating search efforts.

The Nepalese army has rescued more than 100 people from flood-affected areas through helicopter operations on Thursday morning, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said.

At least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to the country’s capital, Kathmandu, he said, adding that army teams also evacuated people trapped inside facilities linked to the Trishuli hydropower project.

In Tibet, a mudslide that struck near the land border crossing of Gyirong Port on Wednesday left mud in the surrounding areas more than 1½ meters (5 feet) deep on average, with some road sections exceeding 2 meters (6 feet), Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported. Roads leading to the port were all damaged, while secondary collapses or landslides might occur as rain continued in the area, it added.

CCTV said that a barrier lake has also been discovered in the direction of the port, posing challenges to the rescue operation. Chinese authorities deployed a large military transport aircraft to send a team to the region, it said.

While electricity supply and communication resumed in the central urban areas in Gyirong town, those linked to the port were cut off, it said.

title: Nepal-Tibet floods: What happened, what caused them and who is missing? - Al Jazeera
description: Nepal-Tibet floods: What happened, what caused them and who is missing?  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
On Wednesday, part of a glacier collapsed high in the Himalayas, triggering catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border.

At least 160 people have been confirmed dead, while nearly 1,500 people are missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet.

Recommended Stories list of 2 items list 1 of 2 Over 160 killed, 800 missing in Nepal after devastating Himalayan floods

Over 160 killed, 800 missing in Nepal after devastating Himalayan floods list 2 of 2 Rescuers search for survivors after Nepal–China floods kill at least 165 end of list

In Nepal, 826 people are missing, including almost 600 foreign tourists, according to police and tourism officials. Across the border, Chinese state media reported that 558 people were missing in Tibet’s Gyirong County, including 260 foreign nationals.

Here is what we know about what triggered the disaster, where the floods struck, and the risks facing the rapidly warming Himalayan region.

What happened in Nepal?

At about 8:40am local time (02:55 GMT) on Wednesday, flash floods and mudslides swept through mountainous areas along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing at least 157 people in Nepal and three in Tibet and leaving nearly 1,500 people missing across the region.

A huge flood of water, mud and rocks swept through the Lhende Khola river valley, engulfing villages and destroying homes and critical infrastructure. At least 19 bridges and about 40km (25 miles) of roads were washed away.

Nepalese soldiers and rescue teams have been deployed with helicopters, drones and search dogs, but high river levels, damaged roads and mud have complicated efforts to reach some of the worst-hit areas.

Across the border in Tibet, deep sediment has also delayed Chinese rescue teams trying to reach the border zone.

What triggered the mudslide and flash floods?

Officials were caught off-guard by the floods on Wednesday because it was not raining, according to local news editors.

Advertisement

The disaster appears to have begun high in the Himalayas, where part of a glacier collapsed, triggering a chain of events that caused a powerful surge of water and debris downstream.

Satellite imagery showed that a substantial section of the lower end of the glacier broke away at an elevation of about 5,200 metres (17,000 feet), plunging about 1,200 metres (3,900ft) onto the valley floor, gathering rock and sediment as it fell.

The resulting ice-rock avalanche struck the Lhende River in Tibet, about 20km (12 miles) northeast of the Nepal-China border crossing. Debris temporarily blocked the river before the natural dam gave way, releasing a powerful flood downstream.

Early reports suggested that a magnitude 4.4 earthquake had triggered the collapse. However, the United States Geological Survey (USGS) later revised its assessment, saying the seismic signal had been generated by the landslide itself rather than an earthquake.

The landslide eventually registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

A drone view shows mud covering properties following the flash flood, in the Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 26, 2026 [Reuters]

Where exactly did the floods happen?

The disaster struck the mountainous Nepal-Tibet border region, with some of the worst damage in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, immediately south of the Chinese border.

The initial surge entered the Lhende Khola, which feeds into the Bhote Koshi and then the Trishuli River, carrying floodwaters south through Nepal. Water levels in the Trishuli reportedly rose by as much as 9 metres (27 ft) in just 30 minutes.

In the Rasuwa district, Timure and Syapru Besi were among the affected settlements. Further downstream, flooding reached parts of Nepal’s Nuwakot and Dhading districts, damaging homes, roads and other infrastructure.

Across the border in Tibet, mud and debris hit Gyirong Port in the Shigatse region.

The Trishuli eventually joins the Narayani River, which crosses into India’s Bihar state, where it is known as the Gandak River.

What do we know about the victims?

At least 160 people have been confirmed dead, while nearly 1,500 remain missing on both sides of the Nepal-Tibet border.

Nepal: Police have recovered at least 157 bodies.

Police have recovered at least 157 bodies. Tibet: Authorities have reported at least three deaths in Gyirong County, where 558 people are missing, including 260 foreign nationals.

“My brother-in-law had a liquor store here. I got a call from him this morning, and they were crying and said their entire house had been swept away,” Raju Bhadel, a local businessman in Nepal, told Al Jazeera.

Advertisement

Manoj Mishra, a teacher, described seeing vehicles and people being carried away by the floodwaters in Nepal. “I saw around nine trucks being swept away by the floods, including people. It’s a heartbreaking incident,” he said.

Damaged houses stand precariously near the swollen, debris-choked banks of the Trishuli River after flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Wednesday [Niranjan Shrestha/AP]

Who is missing?

Nearly 1,500 people are missing across Nepal and Tibet, including at least 800 foreign nationals.

In Nepal, 826 people were reported missing, including almost 600 foreign tourists, according to police and tourism officials. The missing tourists come from more than two dozen countries.

Among those reported missing in Nepal are:

India: 177

177 United States: 63

63 Australia: 34

34 United Kingdom: 33

33 Canada: 25

Authorities have not yet provided a complete nationality breakdown for all the missing foreign nationals.

Across the border, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV said 558 people were missing in Tibet’s Gyirong County, including 260 foreign nationals.

Many of those caught up in the disaster were pilgrims travelling towards Kailash Mansarovar in Tibet. Tourism officials are working to account for groups that had been travelling through the region when the floods struck.

The injured and rescued

At least 65 people were being treated for injuries in local hospitals and in Kathmandu.

More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police personnel have been mobilised for the rescue operation, while helicopters are searching for survivors and delivering emergency supplies to communities cut off by damaged roads and flooding.

Survivors from badly affected areas have also been evacuated by military helicopter, including some taken to hospitals in Kathmandu.

How are international organisations and leaders responding to the crisis?

Countries and international organisations have offered emergency assistance, funding and technical support as rescue operations continue in Nepal and Tibet.

Humanitarian and financial aid

India has sent a rescue aircraft carrying about 10 tonnes of emergency supplies to Nepal, including temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits, solar lamps and medicines.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah and pledged India’s support.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) has released 1 million Swiss francs ($1.2m) in emergency funding to support the Nepal Red Cross Society’s relief operations and damage assessments.

International coordination and satellite support

The United Nations has deployed personnel in Nepal to support government-led relief efforts, while its office in China has said it is ready to assist rescue operations in Tibet.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed his condolences to those affected and said the organisation stood in solidarity with communities hit by the disaster.

The European Union has activated its Copernicus Emergency Management Service, which uses satellite imagery to map disaster zones and provide information that can help authorities assess damage and coordinate rescue operations.

Search-and-rescue efforts

South Korea has established a government task force after several South Korean nationals working at a hydropower project were reported missing. Seoul said it planned to send a rapid-response team involving government, fire and police personnel to Nepal to assist with the search.

Advertisement

The United States said it was sending a disaster response adviser and providing $500,000 in assistance.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada was closely following the situation, describing the floods as “absolutely devastating”.

On the Chinese side, President Xi Jinping ordered an “all-out” search-and-rescue operation for people missing in Tibet and called for efforts to prevent further disasters.

What role did climate change play in this disaster?

Scientists are still investigating what triggered the glacier collapse, and it is too early to determine how much climate change contributed to this specific event.

However, the disaster comes against a backdrop of rapid warming and glacial loss across the Himalayas. Glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya mountain range – which spans Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Pakistan – lost ice 65 percent faster between 2011 and 2020 than during the previous decade. Nepal’s glaciers have lost close to one-third of their ice volume in roughly three decades.

As glaciers retreat, mountain slopes can become increasingly unstable, and meltwater can accumulate in or around glaciers, increasing the potential for sudden floods.

Satellite observations showed unusually warm conditions around the affected glacier before the collapse, with snow cover diminishing considerably and exposing more bare ice.

Researchers are investigating whether melting contributed to the glacier’s instability, but a direct link between climate change and this week’s collapse has not been established.

What is the situation now?

More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police personnel are searching for survivors and recovering bodies, while helicopters are delivering tents, food and other emergency supplies to communities cut off by the floods.

Officials have warned that the death toll is likely to rise as rescuers reach areas that remain inaccessible because of damaged roads, high water levels and thick layers of mud.

In Tibet, Chinese authorities are also monitoring a still-dammed lake upstream from the disaster zone in Gyirong that could complicate rescue efforts and pose a further flood risk.

प्रारंभिक उफान ल्हेंडे खोला में प्रवेश केलक, जे भोटे कोशी आ फेर त्रिशुली नदी में घुसैत अछि, जे बाढ़ के पानि के नेपाल होइत दक्षिण दिस ल जाइत अछि | खबर छै कि त्रिशुली केरऽ पानी केरऽ स्तर महज ३० मिनट म॑ ९ मीटर (२७ फीट) तलक बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

रसुवा जिला मे तैमुरे आ स्याप्रू बेसी प्रभावित बस्ती मे शामिल छल। आगू नीचाँ नेपालक नुवाकोट आ धाडिंग जिलाक किछु हिस्सा मे बाढ़ि पहुँचि गेल जाहि सँ घर, सड़क आ अन्य बुनियादी ढांचा केँ नुकसान पहुँचल।

तिब्बत में सीमा के पार शिगात्से क्षेत्र के ग्यरोंग बंदरगाह पर कीचड़ आ मलबा आबि गेल अछि.

त्रिशूली अंततः नारायणी नदी में मिलैत अछि जे भारत के बिहार राज्य में पार भ जायत अछि, जतय एकरा गंडक नदी के नाम सं जानल जाइत अछि |

पीड़ित के बारे में हमरा सब के की पता अछि?

कम सँ कम १६० गोटेके मृत्यु भेल पुष्टि भेल अछि, जखन कि नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमाक दुनू कात लगभग १५०० गोटे लापता अछि ।

नेपाल : पुलिस कम स कम 157 शव बरामद केलक अछि।

पुलिस कम स कम 157 लाश बरामद क चुकल अछि। तिब्बत : अधिकारि सब ग्योरोंग काउंटी में कम स कम तीन गोटे के मौत के सूचना देलक अछि, जतय 558 लोक लापता छथि, जाहि में 260 विदेशी नागरिक सेहो शामिल छथि।

नेपालक स्थानीय व्यवसायी राजू भदेल अल जजीरा केँ कहलनि जे, हमर देवरक एतय शराबक दोकान छल, आइ भोरे हुनका सँ फोन आयल छल, आ ओ सब कानि रहल छल आ कहैत छल जे हुनकर पूरा घर बहरा गेल अछि।

विज्ञापन

शिक्षक मनोज मिश्र नेपाल मे बाढ़िक पानि सँ वाहन आ लोक केँ बहैत देखबाक वर्णन केलनि। ओ कहला जे हम देखलहुं जे करीब नौटा ट्रक बाढ़ि मे बहैत छल, जाहि मे लोक सेहो शामिल छल। ई एकटा हृदयविदारक घटना अछि।'

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में बुधदिन आघाती बाढ़ के बाद त्रिशुली नदी के सूजल, मलबा स गला घोंटल तट के पास क्षतिग्रस्त घर अनिश्चित रूप स ठाढ़ अछि [निरंजन श्रेष्ठ/एपी]।

के गायब अछि ?

पूरा नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे लगभग 1500 लोक लापता अछि जाहि मे कम सं कम 800 विदेशी नागरिक सेहो शामिल अछि.

नेपालमे लगभग ६०० विदेशी पर्यटक सहित ८२६ गोटे लापता होयबाक सूचना पुलिस आ पर्यटन अधिकारीसभक अनुसार अछि । लापता पर्यटक दू दर्जन स बेसी देश स आबि रहल छथि।

नेपालमे लापता होयबाक सूचना भेटलमे १.

भारत : 177

177 संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका: 63

63 ऑस्ट्रेलिया : 34

34 यूनाइटेड किंगडम: 33

33 कनाडा : 25

अधिकारि सब एखन धरि सब विदेशी नागरिक के पूर्ण राष्ट्रीयता विभाजन के व्यवस्था नै केलक अछि।

सीमा पार चीनी राज्य प्रसारक सीसीटीवी के कहनाय छनि जे तिब्बत के ग्यारोंग काउंटी मे 558 लोक लापता अछि जाहि मे 260 विदेशी नागरिक सेहो शामिल छथिन्ह.

एहि आपदा मे फंसल बहुतो लोक तिब्बत क कैलाश मनसरोवर दिस जा रहल तीर्थयात्री छलाह । पर्यटन अधिकारी ओहि समूह के हिसाब देबय मे काज क रहल छथिन्ह जे बाढ़ि के समय एहि क्षेत्र मे यात्रा क रहल छल.

घायल आ बचाओल गेल

स्थानीय अस्पताल आ काठमाण्डौमे कमसँ कम ६५ गोटेके घायल भेलाक इलाज भऽ रहल छल ।

बचाव अभियान लेल ५ हजार सँ बेसी नेपाली सेना आ प्रहरी जवान जुटाओल गेल अछि, जखन कि हेलीकॉप्टर बचि गेल लोकक खोज मे लागल अछि आ क्षतिग्रस्त सड़क आ बाढ़ि सँ कटल समुदाय मे आपातकालीन आपूर्ति पहुँचा रहल अछि ।

बहुत प्रभावित इलाका स बचि गेल लोक कए सैन्य हेलीकॉप्टर स सेहो निकालल गेल अछि, जाहि मे किछु गोटे कए काठमांडू क अस्पताल पहुंचाओल गेल अछि।

अंतरराष्ट्रीय संगठन आ नेता सब संकट के कोना जवाब द रहल छैथ?

नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे बचाव अभियान जारी रहला पर देश आ अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय संस्था आपातकालीन सहायता, धन आ तकनीकी सहयोग प्रदान केने अछि ।

मानवीय एवं आर्थिक सहायता

भारत अस्थाई आश्रय स्थल, कम्बल, स्वच्छता किट, सौर दीपक आ दवाई सहित लगभग १० टन आपातकालीन सामान ल क बचाव विमान नेपाल पठेलक अछि ।

भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदी नेपालके प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाहसँग बात कए भारतके सहयोगके वचन देलनि ।

नेपाल रेड क्रॉस सोसाइटी केरऽ राहत कार्य आरू क्षति आकलन के समर्थन लेली अंतर्राष्ट्रीय रेड क्रॉस आरू रेड क्रिसेंट सोसाइटी महासंघ (आईएफआरसी) न॑ १० लाख स्विस फ्रैंक (१.२ मिलियन डॉलर) के आपातकालीन फंडिंग जारी करलकै ।

अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समन्वय एवं उपग्रह समर्थन

संयुक्त राष्ट्र नेपालमे सरकारक नेतृत्वमे कएल गेल राहत कार्यके सहयोगके लेल जवान तैनात केने अछि, तहिना चीनमे रहल ओकर कार्यालय तिब्बतमे उद्धार कार्यमे सहयोगके लेल तत्पर रहल बतौने अछि ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासचिव एंटोनियो गुटेरेस नँ प्रभावित लोगऽ के प्रति संवेदना व्यक्त करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै कि संगठन आपदा स॑ प्रभावित समुदायऽ के साथ एकजुटता के साथ खड़ा छै ।

यूरोपीय संघ न॑ अपनऽ कोपर्निकस आपातकालीन प्रबंधन सेवा क॑ सक्रिय करी देल॑ छै, जे उपग्रह केरऽ छवि के उपयोग आपदा क्षेत्रऽ के नक्शा बनाबै लेली करै छै आरू जानकारी उपलब्ध करै छै जे अधिकारियऽ क॑ नुकसान के आकलन करै आरू बचाव अभियान के समन्वय करै म॑ मदद करी सकै छै ।

खोज-बचाव के प्रयास

जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ काम करै वाला दक्षिण कोरिया केरऽ कईएक नागरिकऽ के लापता होय के खबर मिलला के बाद दक्षिण कोरिया न॑ सरकारी टास्क फोर्स के स्थापना करलकै । सियोल के कहनाय छनि जे ओ तलाशी मे सहयोग करय लेल सरकार, फायर आ पुलिस के जवान के शामिल करय वाला रैपिड रिस्पांस टीम के नेपाल भेजय के योजना बना रहल अछि.

विज्ञापन

अमेरिका न॑ कहलकै कि हुनी आपदा प्रतिक्रिया सलाहकार भेजै छै आरू ५ लाख डॉलर के सहायता द॑ रहलऽ छै ।

कनाडा केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री मार्क कार्नी न॑ कहलकै कि कनाडा ई स्थिति केरऽ बारीकी स॑ पालन करी रहलऽ छै आरू बाढ़ क॑ “बिल्कुल विनाशकारी” बतैलकै ।

चीनी तरफऽ स॑ राष्ट्रपति शी जिनपिंग न॑ तिब्बत म॑ लापता लोगऽ लेली “ऑल आउट” खोज-बचाव अभियान के आदेश देलकै आरू आरू आपदा क॑ रोकै के प्रयास करै के आह्वान करलकै ।

एहि आपदा मे जलवायु परिवर्तन क की भूमिका छल?

वैज्ञानिक सब अखनी भी जांच करी रहलऽ छै कि ग्लेशियर केरऽ पतन के कारण की छेलै, आरू ई तय करना बहुत जल्दी छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ ई विशिष्ट घटना म॑ कतेक योगदान छेलै ।

लेकिन, ई आपदा पूरा हिमालय में तेजी सें गर्मी आरू हिमनदी के नुकसान के पृष्ठभूमि में आबी रहलऽ छै । हिन्दू कुश हिमालय पर्वत श्रृंखला केरऽ पूरा ग्लेशियरऽ म॑ – जे अफगानिस्तान, बांग्लादेश, भूटान, चीन, भारत, म्यांमार, नेपाल आरू पाकिस्तान म॑ फैललऽ छै – न॑ २०११ आरू २०२० के बीच पिछला दशक के तुलना म॑ ६५ प्रतिशत तेजी स॑ बर्फ के नुकसान करलकै । नेपाल केरऽ ग्लेशियरऽ म॑ लगभग तीन दशक म॑ अपनऽ बर्फ केरऽ मात्रा के लगभग एक तिहाई हिस्सा के नुकसान होय ​​गेलऽ छै ।

जेना-जेना ग्लेशियर पाछू हटैत अछि, पहाड़क ढलान तेजी सं अस्थिर भ सकैत अछि, आ ग्लेशियर में वा ओकर आसपास पिघलल पानि जमा भ सकैत अछि, जाहि सं अचानक बाढ़िक संभावना बढ़ि सकैत अछि.

उपग्रह केरऽ अवलोकन म॑ गिरै स॑ पहल॑ प्रभावित ग्लेशियर के आसपास असामान्य रूप स॑ गर्म परिस्थिति देखलऽ गेलै, जेकरा म॑ बर्फ केरऽ आवरण काफी कम होय गेलै आरू अधिक नंगे बर्फ उजागर होय गेलै ।

शोधकर्ता सब ई जांच करी रहलऽ छै कि ग्लेशियर केरऽ अस्थिरता म॑ पिघलना के योगदान छेलै कि नै, लेकिन जलवायु परिवर्तन आरू ई सप्ताह केरऽ पतन के बीच सीधा संबंध नै स्थापित करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

आब की स्थिति अछि?

पाँच हजार सँ बेसी नेपाली सेना आ प्रहरी जवान बचि गेल आ बरामद शव के खोज मे लागल अछि, तहिना हेलीकॉप्टर बाढ़ि सँ कटल समुदाय मे टेंट, भोजन आ अन्य आपातकालीन आपूर्ति पहुँचा रहल अछि ।

अधिकारियऽ न॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै कि बचाबै वाला लोगऽ के ऐसनऽ इलाका म॑ पहुँचला स॑ मौतऽ के संख्या बढ़ै के संभावना छै, जे सड़कऽ क॑ क्षतिग्रस्त होय गेलऽ छै, पानी केरऽ स्तर अधिक होय गेलऽ छै आरू कीचड़ के मोटऽ परत के वजह स॑ दुर्गम छै ।

तिब्बत म॑ चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ ग्योरॉंग केरऽ आपदा क्षेत्र स॑ ऊपर एगो झील प॑ भी नजर रखी रहलऽ छै जेकरा स॑ बचाव के प्रयास जटिल होय सकै छै आरू बाढ़ केरऽ आरू खतरा पैदा होय सकै छै ।

title: More than 1,300 missing in Nepal, Tibet after catastrophic floods left little time to flee - WLFI
description: More than 1,300 missing in Nepal, Tibet after catastrophic floods left little time to flee  WLFI

DEVIGHAT, Nepal (AP) - Rescue teams searched on Thursday for hundreds of missing people along the Nepal-China border after a catastrophic and deadly torrent of floods and mud swept through several communities a day earlier following a glacier collapse.

The disaster left 168 people dead and more than 1,300 missing, including foreigners and pilgrims, and displaced hundreds of people across the Himalayan region.

Videos of the tragedy showed the flood swallowing people as they tried to escape, and destroying buildings and bridges. On Thursday, drone footage from Nepal showed the scale of the destruction.

The region’s steep valleys are economic lifelines and travel corridors, but are precarious when disaster strikes. Images showed what appeared to be the second floors of buildings in Nuwakot slathered in mud after the torrent rushed by. Debris hung from tree branches and wires, vehicles were buried and some stunned survivors were caked in mud. The floods halted travel in some areas.

There was little time for anyone to flee.

“When I reached Dhunge bazaar, in half an hour, the flood came and damaged all the market. People were preparing to go to the office then,” resident Shoyam Rajbhandari said. “How many people are missing or dead, we don’t know.”

Rescuers carry a victim of flash flooding to safety along the Trishuli River in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha) (Niranjan Shrestha | AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

Warming climate threatens communities

The Himalayan mountain range spans several countries in South Asia and has many of the world’s highest peaks and remaining glaciers.

The steep slopes and the lush valleys below the Himalayan mountain range are especially vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events. Melting glaciers have become more common because of warming because of human-caused climate change.

Researchers in Kathmandu found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting faster, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000.

Damaged houses and vehicles are seen in the aftermath of flash floods along the Trishuli River in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. (Source: AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

Helicopters deployed as roads were damaged

The disaster has left at least 165 dead and 826 people missing in Nepal, and three dead and 558 missing in Tibet, authorities said.

Nepalese officials said that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometers (25 miles) of roads were damaged, complicating search efforts.

The Nepalese army has rescued more than 100 people from flood-affected areas through helicopter operations on Thursday morning, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said.

At least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to the country’s capital, Kathmandu, he said, adding that army teams also evacuated people trapped inside facilities linked to the Trishuli hydropower project.

Rescuers found bodies about 100 kilometers (60 miles) downstream from the disaster zone in Chitwan district. Dozens of injured people have been transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care.

Bishal Kumar Bhandari, chairman of the Nepal Red Cross Society, said they have shifted focus from rescue to large-scale relief operations in the flood-hit districts. He said that around 1,200 people were displaced from at least three villages.

In Tibet, a mudslide that struck near the land border crossing of Gyirong Port on Wednesday left mud in the surrounding areas more than 1½ meters (5 feet) deep on average, with some road sections exceeding 2 meters (6 feet), Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported. Roads leading to the port were all damaged, while secondary collapses or landslides might occur as rain continued in the area, it added.

CCTV said that a barrier lake has also been discovered in the direction of the port, posing challenges to the rescue operation. Chinese authorities deployed a large military transport aircraft to send a team to the region, it said.

While electricity supply and communication resumed in the central urban areas in Gyirong town, those linked to the port were cut off, it said.

Hundreds of foreigners are missing

Officials in Nepal had earlier said hundreds of foreigners were reported missing, including Indian nationals on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.

Australia’s Foreign Minister Penny Wong told reporters Thursday at least 34 Australians on pilgrimages and hiking tours were missing.

Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry on Thursday said 55 Malaysians in Kathmandu are now unreachable, with severe disruptions to infrastructure hampering efforts to contact them.

New Zealand’s foreign ministry said Thursday that five of the country’s nationals were believed to be in the area and their whereabouts were unclear.

Experts say glacier collapse caused devastating floods

The U.S. Geological Survey first reported a magnitude 4.4 earthquake early Wednesday, about 66 kilometers (41 miles) north of Kathmandu, near the border.

The USGS later updated its analysis to say the seismic event it measured was a magnitude 5.2 glacier collapse that sent debris flowing downstream with catastrophic impact on communities. It said its determination was based on data from nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves and satellite imagery, and that no earthquake had occurred.

Climate experts at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an avalanche from a glacier likely caused Wednesday’s flash flood.

“Hydrological observations indicate the exceptional speed and magnitude of the flood wave,” they said in an emailed statement, noting that water levels at one point on the Trishuli river rose by as much as 9 meters (27 feet) over half an hour.

The Lhende Khola River, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, had maximum flooding, they said.

The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions.

The region saw similar flash floods in August 2025, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

___

Shristi Kafle reported from Kathmandu, Nepal. Kanis Leung in Hong Kong, Aijaz Hussain in Srinagar, India, Rod McGuirk in Melbourne, Australia, Eileen Ng in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and Charlotte Graham-McLay in Wellington, New Zealand, contributed to this report.

एहि आपदा मे विदेशी आ तीर्थयात्री सहित 168 लोकक मौत आ 1300 सं बेसी लोक लापता भ गेल आ पूरा हिमालय क्षेत्र मे सैकड़ों लोक विस्थापित भ गेलाह।

एहि त्रासदी के वीडियो मे देखल गेल जे बाढ़ि लोक के भागय के कोशिश मे निगल गेल, आओर भवन आओर पुल के तबाह क देलक. बृहस्पतिदिन नेपाल सँ ड्रोन फुटेज मे विनाशक पैमाना देखाओल गेल छल ।

ई क्षेत्र केरऽ खड़ा घाटी आर्थिक जीवन रेखा आरू यात्रा गलियारा छै, लेकिन आपदा आबै प॑ अनिश्चित होय जाय छै । छवि में देखल गेल जे नुवाकोट के भवन के दोसर मंजिल बुझाइत छल जे धार के दौड़-धूप के बाद थाल-कादो सं लथपथ भ गेल छल. गाछक डारि आ तार पर मलबा लटकल, गाड़ी गाड़ल आ किछु स्तब्ध बचि गेल लोक थाल मे केक भ गेल। बाढ़ि के कारण किछ इलाका मे यात्रा बंद भ गेल.

ककरो पलायन करबाक समय कम छल।

निवासी शोयम राजभंडारी कहलनि जे, जखन हम ढुंगे बाजार पहुंचलहुं त आधा घंटा मे बाढ़ि आबि कए सबटा बाजार कए नुकसान पहुंचेलक, तखन लोक ऑफिस जेबाक तैयारी मे छल। “कतेक लोक लापता अछि वा मरि गेल अछि, से हमरा सभ केँ नहि बुझल अछि।”

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में त्रिशूली नदी के किनारे फ्लैश फ्लडिंग के शिकार एक को सुरक्षित स्थान पर लेकर बचावकर्मी, बुधवार, 26 अगस्त 2026. (एपी फोटो/निरंजन श्रेष्ठ) (निरंजन श्रेष्ठ | एपी फोटो/निरंजन श्रेष्ठ)

गर्मी बढ़ला सं समुदाय पर खतरा मंडरा रहल अछि

हिमालयी पर्वत श्रृंखला दक्षिण एशिया केरऽ कई देशऽ म॑ फैललऽ छै आरू एकरऽ दुनिया केरऽ बहुत सारा ऊंचऽ चोटी आरू शेष ग्लेशियर छै ।

हिमालयी पर्वत श्रृंखला के नीचे के खड़ा ढलान आरू रसीला घाटी बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन, आरू चरम मौसमी घटना के विशेष रूप स॑ शिकार छै । मानव के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण गर्मी के कारण ग्लेशियर के पिघलना बेसी आम भ गेल अछि ।

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में त्रिशूली नदी के किनारे आघात के बाद क्षतिग्रस्त घर आ वाहन देखल जा रहल अछि, बुध दिन, 26 अगस्त 2026. (स्रोत: एपी फोटो/निरंजन श्रेष्ठ)

सड़क क्षतिग्रस्त भेला पर तैनात हेलीकॉप्टर

एहि आपदामे नेपालमे कमसँ कम १६५ गोटेके मृत्यु आ ८२६ गोटे लापता, आ तिब्बतमे तीन गोटेके मृत्यु आ ५५८ गोटे लापता भेल अधिकारीसब जनौलक अछि ।

दर्जनों पुल नष्ट भ गेल आ लगभग 40 किलोमीटर (25 मील) के सड़क क्षतिग्रस्त भेला स खोज के प्रयास जटिल भ गेल नेपाली अधिकारी बतौलनि।

नेपाली सेना बृहस्पतिदिन भोरमे हेलीकॉप्टर अभियानके माध्यमसँ बाढि प्रभावित क्षेत्रसँ १००सँ बेसी गोटेके उद्धार केने सेना प्रवक्ता ब्रिगेडियर एस. जनरल राजा राम बस्नेट कहलनि।

कम स कम आठ विदेशी नागरिक कए हवाई जहाज स देश क राजधानी काठमांडू पहुंचाओल गेल ओ कहला जे सेना क टीम त्रिशुली जलविद्युत परियोजना स जुड़ल सुविधा क भीतर फंसल लोक कए सेहो बाहर निकालि लेलक।

चितवन जिला के आपदा क्षेत्र स करीब 100 किलोमीटर (60 मील) नीचा बचावकर्मी के लाश भेटल। दर्जनों घायल लोक के उन्नत चिकित्सा के लेल काठमांडू पहुंचाओल गेल अछि.

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीके अध्यक्ष विशाल कुमार भण्डारी बाढिग्रस्त जिल्लामे उद्धारसँ बड पैघ राहत कार्यमे केन्द्रित केने बतौलनि । ओ कहला जे कम स कम तीन गाम स करीब 1200 लोक विस्थापित भ गेल अछि।

चीनी राज्य प्रसारक सीसीटीवी केरऽ रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक तिब्बत म॑ बुधवार क॑ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह केरऽ जमीनी सीमा क्रासिंग के पास कीचड़ गिरला स॑ आसपास के इलाका म॑ औसतन 11⁄2 मीटर (5 फीट) स॑ भी अधिक गहरा कीचड़ पड़लऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ कुछ सड़कऽ के खंड 2 मीटर (6 फीट) स॑ भी अधिक छै । बंदरगाह दिस जाय वाला सड़क सब क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि, जखन कि इलाका मे बरखा जारी रहला स गौण ढहब या भूस्खलन भ सकैत अछि।

सीसीटीवी के कहनाय छनि जे बंदरगाह के दिशा मे एकटा बैरियर झील सेहो भेटल अछि, जाहि सं बचाव अभियान के लेल चुनौती अछि. चीन केरऽ अधिकारियऽ न॑ ई क्षेत्र म॑ टीम भेजै लेली एगो बड़ऽ सैन्य परिवहन विमान तैनात करलकै ।

ग्यरोंग शहर केरऽ मध्य शहरी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ जहां बिजली आपूर्ति आरू संचार फेर स॑ शुरू होय गेलै, वहीं बंदरगाह स॑ जुड़लऽ क्षेत्रऽ म॑ कटौती होय गेलै ।

सैकड़ों विदेशी लापता अछि

नेपाल के अधिकारी सब पहिने बतौने छल जे हिन्दू के लेल पवित्र स्थल तिब्बत के कैलाश पर्वत के तीर्थयात्रा पर निकलल भारतीय नागरिक सहित सैकड़ों विदेशी के लापता होय के खबर अछि।

ऑस्ट्रेलिया केरऽ विदेश मंत्री पेनी वोंग न॑ गुरुवार क॑ पत्रकारऽ स॑ कहलकै कि तीर्थयात्रा आरू पैदल यात्रा प॑ जाय वाला कम स॑ कम ३४ ऑस्ट्रेलियाई गायब छै ।

मलेशिया केरऽ विदेश मंत्रालय न॑ गुरुवार क॑ कहलकै कि काठमांडू म॑ ५५ मलेशियाई लोगऽ के पहुँच अब॑ नै छै, जेकरा चलतें बुनियादी ढाँचा म॑ भारी बाधा के कारण ओकरा स॑ संपर्क करै के प्रयास म॑ बाधा पहुँचै छै ।

न्यूजीलैंड केरऽ विदेश मंत्रालय न॑ गुरुवार क॑ कहलकै कि देश केरऽ पांच नागरिकऽ के ई क्षेत्र म॑ होय के आशंका छै आरू ओकरऽ ठिकाना साफ नै छै ।

विशेषज्ञ के कहनाय छनि जे ग्लेशियर के गिरला सं विनाशकारी बाढ़ि आयल

अमेरिकी भूवैज्ञानिक सर्वेक्षण न॑ सबसें पहलऽ बुधवार के सुबह काठमांडू स॑ लगभग ६६ किलोमीटर (४१ मील) उत्तर म॑ सीमा के पास ४.४ तीव्रता के भूकंप के खबर देल॑ छेलै ।

बाद म॑ यूएसजीएस न॑ अपनऽ विश्लेषण क॑ अपडेट करी क॑ कहलकै कि ओकरा द्वारा मापलऽ गेलऽ भूकंपीय घटना ५.२ परिमाण के ग्लेशियर केरऽ पतन छेलै जेकरा स॑ मलबा नीचें बह॑ लगलै जेकरऽ समुदायऽ प॑ विनाशकारी प्रभाव पड़ै छै । ओकरा न॑ कहलकै कि ओकरऽ निर्धारण नजदीकी भूकंपीय स्टेशन, लंबा समय तलक के भूकंपीय तरंग आरू उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी के आंकड़ा के आधार प॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू कोय भूकंप नै ऐलऽ छै ।

काठमांडू स्थित इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट के जलवायु विशेषज्ञ के कहनाय छनि जे ग्लेशियर सं हिमस्खलन सं बुधदिन आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के कारण संभव अछि.

ईमेल द्वारा जारी बयान मँ हुनी कहलकै, “जलशास्त्रीय अवलोकन बाढ़ के लहर के असाधारण गति आरू परिमाण के संकेत दै छै ।

ओ सब कहलनि जे, भोटेकोशी के सहायक नदी ल्हेंडे खोला नदी मे बेसी स बेसी बाढ़ि आयल।

नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे आयल आपदा एक बेर के नहि अछि. तेजी स॑ अस्थिर होय रहलऽ हिमालयी बर्फ प्रणाली स॑ दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ घन आबादी वाला क्षेत्रऽ म॑ स॑ एक क्षेत्र म॑ समुदाय, बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू पानी के आपूर्ति प॑ खतरा मंडरा रहलऽ छै ।

ई क्षेत्र म॑ अगस्त २०२५ म॑ भी ऐसनऽ ही आकस्मिक बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छेलै, जब॑ तिब्बत केरऽ एगो हिमनदी झील म॑ अधिक तापमान के वजह स॑ पानी भरलऽ छेलै । नौ गोटेक मृत्यु भेल अछि, आ नेपाल आ चीन केँ जोड़य बला पुल सहित महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढांचा क्षतिग्रस्त भेल अछि ।

___ २.

नेपालक काठमाण्डौसँ श्रीस्टी काफ्लेक सूचना। ई रिपोर्ट म॑ हांगकांग म॑ कानिस लेउंग, भारत केरऽ श्रीनगर म॑ ऐजाज हुसैन, ऑस्ट्रेलिया केरऽ मेलबर्न म॑ रोड मैकगुइर्क, मलेशिया केरऽ कुआलालंपुर म॑ एलीन एनजी आरू न्यूजीलैंड केरऽ वेलिंगटन म॑ शार्लोट ग्राहम-मैकले न॑ योगदान देलकै ।

A line drawn on a map. A barricade parked on a road. Barbed wire. And an iron gate. All of this can divide nations, and draw boundaries, but not nature. Nature does not recognise fences. It moves freely across human-made political lines. Nature knows no borders. So, when a massive flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse hit the neighbouring Nepal, it triggered alerts in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Why? It is the Gandak River that transcends all borders and flows between the two nations.

Nepal To India, Narayani To Gandak Rivers

In Nepal, it is Narayani, and by the time it reaches India, the river is called Gandak. It is the same river that flows from Nepal into India.

The Narayani river originates near the Tibet-Nepal border and enters Nepal from the Mustang region. Crossing the Indo-Nepal border at Triveni Dham, the river reaches Valmikinagar in Bihar.

"From Valmikinagar, Gandak winds its way through the states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar before merging into the Ganga at Hajipur and Sonepur," according to the Living Waters Museum report.

A rise in water levels in Nepal's Narayani would be reflected downstream in India's Gandak. Therefore, eastern Uttar Pradesh and northern Bihar face an escalated flood risk. Other major rivers flowing from Nepal into Uttar Pradesh include the Ghaghara (Karnali), Sharda (Kali), and Rapti.

UP, Bihar On High Alert

In Bihar, special vigilance has been ordered in West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali, besides other vulnerable districts such as Sitamarhi and Sheohar.

All 36 gates of Gandak barrage, situated at Valmikinagar in West Champaran, the northernmost district of Bihar that shares a border with Nepal, were opened on Wednesday to help control the situation.

Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary, who also holds the Water Resources Department (WRD) portfolio, said, "The department has taken immediate precautionary measures. All 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage at Valmikinagar have been opened, and a technical team led by a Superintending Engineer has been deployed at the barrage. Warnings have also been issued to all districts in the Gandak river basin."

The opening of barrage gates can facilitate the flow of water.

Around 86,000 cusecs of water were discharged from the Gandak Barrage at Valmikinagar around Wednesday noon.

"In view of the rising water levels in the Gandak and Narayani rivers and the possibility of flooding in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts due to its impact, instructions have been issued to the local administration to remain fully vigilant and ensure necessary preparations," Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath posted on X.

In Kushinagar, the district administration has ordered evacuations from Marchahwa, Shivpur and other villages, and announcements are being made urging residents to move to safer locations.

title: East Bay Nepalese community worried after catastrophic floods near Nepal and China border - NBC Bay Area
description: East Bay Nepalese community worried after catastrophic floods near Nepal and China border  NBC Bay Area
publisher.title: NBC Bay Area
full_article:
More than 100 people are dead following the catastrophic flooding near the border of Nepal and China, and a Bay Area man from the impacted area is fearing the worst.

The East Bay has a big Nepalese community, especially in Richmond, were a cultural celebration was held with worry looming over it.

Watch NBC Bay Area News free wherever you are WATCH HERE

Videos coming from near the Nepal and China border are unimaginable, and those videos have been watched by most people at the Richmond gathering.

“A lot of my friends are not founded yet, so they are missing,” said Janak Raj Dhungana, who is from the devastated area. “I’m sure they are not coming back again.”

The country’s police service said at least 157 have been killed, but that number expected to rise in the days to come.

Crews now begin the desperate search for survivors and that includes hundreds of tourists and dozens from the U.S.

“The problem is this is a very big time for tourist who go to Tibet so right now this is a main route that people travel for Nepal to Tibet,” Former Nepal Trek Guide Lhakpa Gelu Sherpa said. “One of the reasons it’s very popular it’s very close to Kathmandu.”

Local social media 59 minutes ago What we know about the changes Meta will roll out for teens and parents Santa Clara 11 hours ago Deadly crash shuts down northbound Montague Expressway in Santa Clara

What caused the colossal disaster wasn’t immediately clear, but climate experts in the country say an avalanche from a glacier most likely prompted the flash flood. The USGS also reported a 4.4 magnitude quake in the area.

This came at the same time Hindus, who make up the biggest religion in Nepal, celebrate a festival for renewal and spiritual protection.

Folks attending Wednesday’s event said this festival is a bittersweet one.

“It’s really hard because we can just pray for them. We cannot do anything,” Dhungana said.

ई ओही समय भेल जखन नेपालक सबसँ पैघ धर्मक गठन करयवला हिन्दू नवीकरण आ आध्यात्मिक रक्षाक लेल उत्सव मनाबैत छथि ।

बुधदिन के आयोजन मे शामिल लोक के कहनाय छनि जे ई महोत्सव मीठ मीठ अछि.

धुंगना कहलनि जे, ई सचमुच कठिन अछि किएक त’ हम सब हुनका लेल बस प्रार्थना क’ सकैत छी, हम सब किछु नहि क’ सकैत छी।

title: EU sends help as Nepal flood kills 165, hundreds of tourists remain missing - RFI
description: EU sends help as Nepal flood kills 165, hundreds of tourists remain missing  RFI
publisher.title: RFI
full_article:
Advertising Read more

A wall of mud and rock on Wednesday collapsed into a river near Gyirong at the border between the Tibet and Nepal, triggering a flash flood that swept through towns and villages, washed way houses, roads and power projects.

At least 165 people have been reported dead, 162 in Nepal and three in Tibet. Nepal's disaster agency said 826 people were unaccounted for on Thursday, among them at least 579 Nepali and foreign tourists.

Tourists from all over the world

Hikers and climbers from around the world travel to Nepal to climb some of the world's highest peaks, including Mount Everest.

The French foreign ministry said 80 French nationals had registered their presence in Nepal. It added that other French people travelling through the country could also be in the affected areas.

“The top priority is to mobilise all available resources to search for and rescue missing people, evacuate and relocate residents in danger, provide prompt medical treatment to the injured and minimise the number of casualties,” Chinese President Xi Jinping said, according to state media.

The Chinese president does not usually comment on disasters unless the death toll is significant.

Chinese authorities have mobilised more than 1,500 personnel.

Aid coming in

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in Nepal said it has released just over €1 million in emergency funds to support rescue operations and provide drinking water and supplies such as blankets, first-aid kits, stretchers and body bags.

The European Union has activated its Copernicus satellite system to support rescue efforts and said it was ready to provide further assistance.

Neighbouring India will be providing military helicopters to help the search and rescue operations, and has sent 10 tonnes of humanitarian aid, including blankets, solar lamps and medicines.

Collapsed glacier

The flooding appears linked to a collapsing glacier.

Nepal's foreign minister initially said an earthquake may have triggered a landslide that blocked the Lhende Khola river and sent water downstream. The US Geological Survey later said the seismic activity initially was actually caused by a glacial collapse and debris flow.

The flooding “was caused by an avalanche of ice that fell into the Lhende River, but its exact cause remains to be confirmed,” Qianggong Zhang, a scientist at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development based in Kathmandu, told the AFP news agency.

Water levels in the Trishuli river, downstream from the blockage, reportedly rose by as much as 9 metres in just 30 minutes.

The blockage is still there and could create further flooding.

चीनी अधिकारी 1500 स बेसी जवान कए जुटा लेलक अछि।

सहायता आबि रहल अछि

नेपाल केरऽ इंटरनेशनल फेडरेशन आफ रेड क्रॉस आरू रेड क्रिसेंट सोसाइटी न॑ कहलकै कि बचाव अभियान म॑ सहायता लेली आरू पेयजल आरू कंबल, प्राथमिक चिकित्सा किट, स्ट्रेचर आरू बॉडी बैग जैसनऽ आपूर्ति उपलब्ध करै लेली १० लाख यूरो स॑ कुछ अधिक के आपातकालीन कोष जारी करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

यूरोपीय संघ न॑ बचाव प्रयासऽ म॑ सहयोग लेली अपनऽ कोपर्निकस उपग्रह प्रणाली क॑ सक्रिय करी क॑ कहलकै कि हुनी आरू सहायता दै लेली तैयार छै ।

पड़ोसी देश भारत खोज आरू बचाव अभियान मँ मदद लेली सैन्य हेलीकॉप्टर उपलब्ध कराबै वाला छै, आरू कंबल, सौर लैंप आरू दवाई सहित १० टन मानवीय सहायता भेजलकै ।

ढह गेल ग्लेशियर

बाढ़ि एकटा ढहैत ग्लेशियर सं जुड़ल बुझाइत अछि.

नेपालके विदेश मन्त्री प्रारंभमे कहलनि जे भूकम्पसँ भूस्खलन भेल होयत जाहिसँ ल्हेन्डे खोला नदी जाम भऽ पानि नीचाँ पठा देल गेल अछि । बाद मँ अमेरिकी भूवैज्ञानिक सर्वेक्षण नँ कहलकै कि ई भूकंपीय गतिविधि शुरू मँ वास्तव मँ हिमनदी के पतन आरू मलबा के बहाव के कारण छेलै ।

काठमांडू स्थित इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट के वैज्ञानिक कियांगगोंग झांग नँ एएफपी समाचार एजेंसी क बतैलकै कि बाढ़ “लेन्डे नदी मँ गिरलौ बर्फ के हिमस्खलन के वजह स॑ भेलै, लेकिन एकरऽ सही कारण के पुष्टि अभी बाकी छै ।

खबर छै कि रुकावट स॑ नीचें स्थित त्रिशुली नदी म॑ महज ३० मिनट म॑ पानी केरऽ स्तर ९ मीटर तलक बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

title: What caused the catastrophic flash flood in Nepal and Tibet – and how does a glacier collapse? - The Guardian
description: What caused the catastrophic flash flood in Nepal and Tibet – and how does a glacier collapse?  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Nepal flash floods: what we know so far On Wednesday morning local time, a landslide of ice and rock resulted in a torrent of mud, water and debris bursting the banks of the Trishuli river, also known as the Bhotekoshi, which runs between China and Nepal. Homes, roads, bridges and power plants were swept away. Officials in Nepal said 403 people, including 341 from foreign countries including India, the US, the UK, Australia, South Korea and Malaysia, have been reported missing. In Tibet, China’s state broadcaster said at least three people were killed and 265 were missing. Experts at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said water levels on the Trishuli river rose by as much as nine meters in half an hour. The Lhende Khola river, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, was most affected, they said. “The Lhende Khola has flooded twice in 14 months, this time triggered by an ice rock avalanche from a glacier on the Nepal side that blocked the river and released a sudden surge downstream,” said Saswata Sanyal, a disaster risk reduction specialist at the climate research group. Map of where the glacial collapse occurred

What caused the flooding in Nepal? An avalanche from a glacier is believed to be the likely cause of the flash flooding. Local media reported Nepal’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, told the country’s parliament on Wednesday that initial reports suggested the floods could have been caused by an earthquake in the ⁠area that triggered a landslide. However, the US Geological Survey (USGS) said that while the event was initially reported to be caused by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, further analysis showed the “seismic event was a glacial collapse and debris flow that caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream” and “no earthquake had occurred”. Deadly flash flood shown sweeping through valley toward village in Nepal – video The USGS noted the glacial collapse had registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event on the Richter scale, occurring near the border between Nepal and China at 8.37am local time on Wednesday. According to Assoc Prof Daniel Shugar, a geomorphologist at the University of Calgary in Canada, initial satellite analysis showed a 0.2 sq km chunk of ice “collapsed about 1.2km vertically”. “What I can see in … satellite imagery from Planet Labs, the lower part of a glacier broke off at about 5,200 metres and crashed onto the valley floor about 1,200 metres below,” he wrote on Bluesky. The satellite imagery also seemed to show that a large ‌amount of snow had melted in the 24 hours prior to the disaster, he said. “Some of the glaciers in the valley were covered in snow yesterday and today they are mostly bare ice. So in other words (and I haven’t seen any weather station data yet), it was probably warm.” Shugar said construction could also be a factor. Prof Andrew Mackintosh, a glaciologist at Monash University in Melbourne, said it was unclear whether the collapse was isolated to the glacier, or was the “whole mountainside collapsing that included part of the glacier”. “When a glacier of that scale collapses, it generates a lot of water, and then there’s a cascading sequence of events … where the water and the sediment combine and bulks up and creates the flood.” An international group of glacier researchers has said that while a glacial collapse was “certainly involved”, it was “unlikely to be the sole cause”.

प्रभाव पड़लै” आरू “कोय भूकंप नै घटलै” । नेपाल केरऽ गाँव के तरफ घाटी के माध्यम स॑ घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ दिखालऽ गेलऽ छै – वीडियो यूएसजीएस न॑ नोट करलकै कि हिमनदी केरऽ पतन रिक्टर पैमाना प॑ ५.२ तीव्रता के title: Nepal floods: More than 160 killed, nearly 1,400 missing - DW.com
description: Nepal floods: More than 160 killed, nearly 1,400 missing  DW.com

full_article:
The death toll from catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and Tibet has risen to at least 165, while nearly 1,400 people were missing.

Rescue teams were searching for survivors on Thursday, a day after a glacial collapse sent a huge wall of mud and rock barreling through the Himalayan communities, sweeping way entire villages.

Devastating flash floods hit northern Nepal To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said 826 people were missing in the country, almost 600 of them foreign nationals.

In Tibet, Chinese broadcaster CCTV reported 558 people missing in Gyirong county, including 260 foreigners. Three deaths had been confirmed there as of Thursday morning, with two villagers rescued.

What do we know about the flood in Nepal and Tibet?

The disaster struck Wednesday when a glacial collapse triggered a flood in the Lhende Khola river, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, in a corridor popular with trekkers and pilgrims connecting Kathmandu with Lhasa.

Nepal police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told Reuters the death toll was expected to keep climbing: "This will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered."

Among those missing in Nepal were large numbers of foreign tourists.

Sunil Sharma, a tourism board spokesperson, told the AP news agency that 133 of the missing were Indian pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a site sacred to Hindus, alongside 47 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons and 24 Canadians.

Reuters cited a slightly different breakdown from police and tourism officials, putting the missing tourists at 177 from India, 63 from the United States, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada.

Survivors describe scale of destruction

As the scale of the disaster became apparent on Thursday, locals recounted a torrent of mud rushing toward them.



"As it got closer, it kept rising higher and higher. When I saw it enter our home, I tried to grab my wife's hand and take her to the terrace. But she was swept away by the mud," Keshav Prasad Baral, a 68-year-old survivor, told Reuters.

He was rescued by helicopter four hours later. "My wife is still somewhere beneath the mud."

"She's gone," he said.



Sagar Pandey, who heads a Himalayan tourism operator, surveyed the area by helicopter and saw that entire settlements had vanished.



"There are no human-made things, no human settlement left. Everything is just flat. So anyone in the hotel, the restaurant, or the car, I believe that everybody is gone," he told Reuters.



More than 5,000 army and police personnel have been mobilized in Nepal, according to army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet. They were using helicopters to drop supplies, including tents, food and more, donated by India to communities cut off by the disaster.

Many of the missing are foreigners visiting for treks or religious pilgrimages Image: Subaas Shrestha/NurPhoto/picture alliance

What caused the flood in Nepal and Tibet?

The US Geological Survey initially recorded the event as a magnitude-4.4 earthquake near the border. But USGS later said it was seismic energy generated by the collapse of glacial rock and ice, rather than an earthquake.



Climate scientists at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development told the AP that an ice-rock avalanche likely dammed the river before releasing a sudden surge.



"The Lhende Khola has flooded twice in 14 months, this time triggered by an ice-rock avalanche from a glacier on the Nepal side that blocked the river and released a sudden surge downstream," said Saswata Sanyal, a disaster risk specialist at the group, stressing the need for early-warning systems in "a warming Himalaya."



A similar flood in the same river system killed nine people in August last year, when high temperatures led to a glacial lake in Tibet overflowing.

Nepal's Nuwakot district was nearly completed covered with mud Image: Navesh Chitrakar/REUTERS

नेपाल मे लापता मे भारी संख्या मे विदेशी पर्यटक सेहो शामिल छल।

पर्यटन बोर्ड केरऽ प्रवक्ता सुनील शर्मा न॑ एपी समाचार एजेंसी क॑ बतैलकै कि लापता म॑ स॑ १३३ भारतीय तीर्थयात्री छै जे हिन्दू लेली पवित्र स्थल तिब्बत केरऽ माउंट कैलाश के यात्रा करी रहलऽ छेलै, जेकरा म॑ ४७ अमेरिकी, ३४ ऑस्ट्रेलियाई, ३३ ब्रिटिश आरू २४ कनाडाई छेलै ।

रायटर न॑ पुलिस आरू पर्यटन अधिकारियऽ स॑ कनी अलग टूटना के हवाला देलकै, जेकरा म॑ लापता पर्यटकऽ के संख्या भारत स॑ १७७, अमेरिका स॑ ६३, ऑस्ट्रेलिया स॑ ३४, ब्रिटेन स॑ ३३ आरू कनाडा स॑ २५ छै ।

गुरुवार कए जेना-जेना आपदा क पैमाना साफ होइत गेल, स्थानीय लोक हुनका दिस दौड़ैत थाल क धार क गप केलथि।



68 वर्षीय बचि गेल केशव प्रसाद बरल रायटर के कहलनि जे, जहिना-जहिना ई नजदीक आबि रहल छल, ओ ऊपर उठैत गेल, जखन हम एकरा हमरा सबहक घर मे प्रवेश करैत देखलहुं त हम अपन पत्नी के हाथ पकड़ि क छत पर ल जेबाक कोशिश केलहुं।मुदा ओ थाल बहरा गेल।

चारि घंटाक बाद हेलीकॉप्टरसँ बचाओल गेल। "हमर पत्नी एखनो कतहु थाल-कादोक नीचाँ छथि।"

ओ कहलनि जे, ओ चलि गेलीह।



हिमालय के पर्यटन संचालक के प्रमुख सागर पांडेय हेलीकॉप्टर सं एहि इलाका के सर्वेक्षण केलनि त देखलनि जे पूरा बस्ती गायब भ गेल अछि.



रायटर स बातचीत मे ओ कहला जे एहि ठाम कोनो मानव निर्मित चीज नहि अछि, कोनो मानव बस्ती नहि बचल अछि। सब किछु बस सपाट अछि।त होटल, रेस्टोरेंट, या गाड़ी मे जे कियो अछि, हमर मानब अछि जे सब कियो चलि गेल अछि।



नेपालमे ५ हजारसँ बेसी सेना आ प्रहरी जवान जुटाओल गेल सेना प्रवक्ता राजा राम बस्नेत जनौलक अछि । ई सब हेलीकॉप्टर के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ टेंट, खाना आरू बहुत कुछ सहित सामान छोड़ी रहलऽ छेलै, जेकरा भारत द्वारा आपदा स॑ कटलऽ समुदायऽ क॑ दान करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे बाढ़िक कारण की भेल?

अमेरिकी भूवैज्ञानिक सर्वेक्षण न॑ शुरू म॑ ई घटना क॑ सीमा के पास ४.४ तीव्रता के भूकंप के रूप म॑ दर्ज करलकै । लेकिन बाद म॑ यूएसजीएस न॑ कहलकै कि ई भूकंप के बजाय हिमनदीय चट्टान आरू बर्फ के गिरला स॑ पैदा होय वाला भूकंपीय ऊर्जा छेकै ।



काठमांडू स्थित इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट केरऽ जलवायु वैज्ञानिक न॑ एपी क॑ बतैलकै कि बर्फ-चट्टानऽ के हिमस्खलन स॑ संभव छै कि अचानक उफान छोड़ै स॑ पहल॑ नदी प॑ बांध होय गेलऽ छै ।



समूह केरऽ आपदा जोखिम विशेषज्ञ सस्वता सन्याल न॑ कहलकै कि १४ महीना म॑ दू बार ल्हेंदे खोला म॑ बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ ई बार नेपाल तरफ के ग्लेशियर स॑ बर्फ के चट्टान के हिमस्खलन के वजह स॑ शुरू होय गेलऽ छै जेकरा स॑ नदी क॑ बंद करी देलऽ गेलै आरू अचानक नीचें के लहर छोड़लऽ गेलै ।



पिछला साल अगस्त म॑ भी यही नदी प्रणाली म॑ ऐसनऽ ही बाढ़ म॑ नौ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छेलै, जब॑ उच्च तापमान के वजह स॑ तिब्बत केरऽ एगो हिमनदी झील म॑ पानी भरलऽ छेलै ।

title: More than 1,300 missing in Nepal and China after deadly Himalayan flood - Al Jazeera
description: More than 1,300 missing in Nepal and China after deadly Himalayan flood  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
More than 1,300 people, including more than 700 foreign nationals, are missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet region after a huge collapse of mud and rock into a Himalayan river triggered catastrophic flooding across local towns and valleys, authorities have said.

Nepalese police and tourism officials confirmed on Thursday that nearly 500 foreigners were among 826 people missing in Nepal. Police added that they expected the confirmed death toll to rise significantly past 165.

“This will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered,” police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle said.

Among the missing tourists from more than two dozen countries, 177 are from India, 63 from the United States, 34 from Australia, 33 from the United Kingdom, and 25 from Canada.

Across the border in Tibet’s Gyirong county, 558 people are reported missing, including 260 foreign nationals, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

Rescuers in Nepal have deployed helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands of people cut off in a rugged mountainous area popular with trekkers and pilgrims travelling between Lhasa in Tibet and the Nepalese capital, Kathmandu.

Video footage verified by news agencies showed rapid torrents of water and debris sweeping away dozens of people at a border crossing in Gyirong, while downstream in Nepal, homes, roads, and power infrastructure were destroyed.

Army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said helicopters were dropping tents, food, and medicine provided by neighbouring India into the hardest-hit districts. More than 5,000 army and police rescue personnel joined the rescue effort that retrieved 125 people on Thursday, including 20 foreigners, he said.

Advertisement

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah left by road for Bidur in one of the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot, to assess the flood situation, his office said on social media.

A drone view shows mud covering buildings and property following devastating floods at Trishuli in Nuwakot district, Nepal, on August 27, 2026 [Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters]

Early reports from Nepalese officials suggested an earthquake in the area may have caused the lower section of a glacier to collapse, triggering the flash floods.

However, the US Geological Survey noted that the seismic event, initially recorded as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, was actually the seismic energy generated by the sudden collapse of glacial rock and ice, followed by a huge debris flow.

Chinese authorities warned that a still-dammed lake in Gyirong, upstream from the flood-affected border crossing, poses further risks and could severely complicate rescue efforts in the area, CCTV reported.

Many of those caught in the disaster were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, high-altitude sites in Tibet revered by Hindus, Buddhists, and followers of other faiths.

Some 77 Hindu pilgrims were at the Nepal-China border immigration office when the flood hit on Wednesday, popular Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru, whose real name is Jagdish Vasudev, said in a video message from Tibet on his social media accounts.

The pilgrims were part of several Hindu groups organised by the Isha Foundation of Sadhguru, who had been visiting Mount Kailash.

“Literally, the entire group was there in the building; this is a terrible and extraordinary event,” he said.

International response

The US State Department announced it was dispatching a disaster response adviser and providing $500,000 in emergency aid.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the flooding as “devastating”, adding that Canadian officials were monitoring the situation closely.

United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres confirmed that UN teams were delivering emergency supplies and support staff to affected communities in Nepal.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese noted that gathering clear information from the remote area remained challenging due to limited local infrastructure and resources.

Sagar Pandey, chief executive of a Himalayan tourism operator, said 15 Indian-Australian pilgrims travelling with his company were among the missing.

“There are no human-made structures, no human settlements left. Everything is just flat,” he said after conducting an aerial survey of the disaster zone. “Anyone in the hotels, restaurants, or vehicles – I believe everyone is gone.”

Damaged houses following devastating floods in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, on August 27, 2026 [Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters]

CCTV footage from the Chinese side of the border showed residents fleeing as a surge of mud, rocks, and floodwater submerged buildings and vehicles.

Advertisement

Preliminary satellite imagery analysis by Planet Labs indicated that a landslide of ice and rock triggered a debris-laden surge down the Lhende River, approximately 20km (12 miles) northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border crossing between Nepal and China.

In the affected valleys, thick mud swathed homes, trees, and vehicles, while aerial footage showed collapsed houses, submerged cars, and a metallic bridge washed away by the torrents.

“There is devastation everywhere we look,” said Tula Bahadur BK, a healthcare worker in Rasuwa. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.”

नेपालक पुलिस आ पर्यटन अधिकारी बृहस्पतिदिन पुष्टि केलथि जे नेपाल मे लापता ८२६ गोटे मे लगभग ५०० विदेशी सेहो शामिल अछि । पुलिस के कहनाय छनि जे हुनका उम्मीद अछि जे पुष्टि भेल मौत के संख्या 165 सं काफी बढ़ि जाएत.
